Subject: Geobinding exception request and ops evidence

Hi Avery / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — we're progressing toward a contractual decision but need a few clarifications on residency and transient cross-border processing before we can sign. Short list of asks from Ops / Privacy:

1) Commitment scope: can Redwood provide a written regional-binding commitment for APAC (Sydney region) and EU (Frankfurt) for our production namespace? If not, what is the strictest guarantee you offer for hosted customers?

2) Temporary failover/replication windows: we expect some replication for DR/backup and periodic geo-syncs. Please describe the maximum duration per incident and cumulative monthly exposure for any cross-border egress from APAC -> EU or US. We need both default behavior and configurable options.

3) KMS & keys: where are encryption keys stored for hosted customers? Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in APAC? If not, where are master keys located?

4) Subprocessor roster & audit evidence: provide the current subprocessor list and, if possible, a 1–2 page sample audit log showing an egress event (sanitized) and the associated timestamp/region headers.

We've attached our internal security questionnaire (GlobeApps_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). Can you get back with a draft commitment and evidence by EOD Feb 25? Also propose a 45-minute technical call to walk through the topology and any gaps (we prefer UTC-friendly times).

Thanks,
--
Ravi Patel
Lead, Platform Ops — GlobeApps
ops@globeapps.com

From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Geobinding exception request and ops evidence

Ravi — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers first, then next steps.

- Regional-binding options: Redwood offers three serving modes: Hosted (standard), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For Hosted customers we provide "region-affinity" with strong default routing to the selected region. For contractual region-binding you can choose Dedicated or Private; for Hosted we can provide a written AZ/region affinity SLA plus documented bounded-failover policies.

- Temporary failover/replication: our standard bounded-failover for hosted customers is configurable; default is a maximum of 120 minutes per incident, with an operational cap of 4 hours of cumulative cross-region sync per 30-day window unless otherwise negotiated. Dedicated/Private options can reduce this to negotiated values (including zero).

- KMS & BYOK: hosted encryption uses customer-region KMS where available. BYOK (customer-managed keys) is supported for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with provider keys but can escrow a key for region-specific encryption in some APAC regions — we'll confirm exact availability for your Sydney tenancy.

- Subprocessors & audit logs: we'll provide the current subprocessor roster and a sanitized audit log sample showing an egress event, with region and timestamp headers.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach a short draft regional commitment (redwood_regional_commitment_draft.pdf) that maps each commitment to hosting mode.
- Marissa (Legal) will follow up on DPA addendum language.
- Can we schedule a technical call? I'm available Mon/Tue next week between 14:00–20:00 UTC.

I'll attach the draft now; we'll follow up with the roster and audit sample within 48 hours.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Strategic Partnerships — Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_regional_commitment_draft.pdf (application/pdf, 2 pages)

Ravi — looping in legal and commercial notes. We're happy to include a region-binding addendum; a few legal guardrails we'd like to propose so the language is actionable:

1) "No systematic cross-border processing": propose to define this as "no routine replication or processing outside the customer-selected region other than bounded failover events as defined below."

2) "Bounded failover event": propose limiting per-event transient egress to 120 minutes (2 hours) and cumulative monthly cross-region exposure to 4 hours for hosted by default. For Dedicated/Private customers this default can be reduced to zero. Any deviation must be documented in incident postmortem and logged.

3) Notification & auditability: Redwood will notify customer within 30 minutes of any bounded failover event and provide an audit package (audit-log-sample.txt plus region headers) within 48 hours.

4) KMS: for Hosted customers, keys are regional where supported; BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private. If GlobeApps requires BYOK for Hosted, we need to scope Dedicated or Private deployment.

I'll attach the subprocessor roster and a CSV for your review. Please confirm if the proposed per-event and monthly caps meet your internal risk tolerance; if not, we can table a commercial uplift for stricter caps.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial & Legal — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Hi Ravi / team — Neha from Infra here. Quick technical notes before our call (and attaching the audit sample):

- KMS residency: for your hosted tenancy in APAC (Sydney) we currently provision envelope keys in-region where the cloud provider exposes a regional KMS. The master root for hosted customers is held in the cloud region (Sydney) for supported providers; for providers that do not yet expose regional keys we keep control-plane keys in a nearby region (e.g., Singapore) but all data-encryption operations for your tenancy will use the in-region envelope keys.

- BYOK: Supported for Dedicated/Private only. If GlobeApps signs Dedicated we can bind a customer-managed key (BYOK) in APAC and provide lifecycle logs. For Hosted we can offer escrowed key material and additional attestation under a commercial addendum, but this is not equivalent to true BYOK.

- Transient replication behavior: Redis KV cache and prefix cache replicate asynchronously for warm-start across a bounded failover partner. Our default bounded-failover configuration for Hosted is: per-incident cross-region sync window up to 120 minutes, cumulative cross-region sync not to exceed 4 hours per 30 days. During the sync we preserve per-request session tokens and KV-IDs; all traffic is over TLS 1.3 with mTLS to the failover peer.

- Audit sample: attached audit-log-sample.txt (sanitized). Key columns: timestamp, tenant_id, event_type, source_region, destination_region, bytes_transferred, trigger_type. Example event included shows a 00:34 minute window for a cache warm-up that flowed APAC -> EU during a DR test.

We'll bring a network diagram and the lifecycle logs to the call. Proposed time: Mon Feb 23 15:00 UTC works for us — confirm and I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
